Why Plain RAG Still Wins

By Ada Example

Retrieval-augmented generation keeps coming back. In this post we look at why plain dense retrieval over the raw conversation beats elaborate memory systems on most long-term memory benchmarks, and what that means for agents you build today. The short version is that rewriting history into memory entries loses the details that matter.

The setup

We compared four systems on LoCoMo and LongMemEval. Each system got the same reader model and the same budget. The only difference was how past turns were stored and retrieved. Details are in the appendix, which we kept short on purpose.

SystemScore
Raw RAG74.5first

Memory layers tend to summarize. Summaries drop the relations and dependency paths that sit behind an answer, so even with complete access to the transformed store, the reader answers less accurately than with the raw evidence. Before adding a memory layer to your agent, run this baseline on your own data.

score = retrieve(history, query) |> rerank |> read

Thanks for reading. If you liked this, the follow-up covers how reranking changes the picture when the history grows past a few thousand turns, and why chunk size matters more than embedding model choice.
